conventions.convention: Modules are unital left modules; tensor products are algebraic over the field k. The tensor action is h·(v⊗w)=Σh₍₁₎v⊗h₍₂₎w, and the unit module acts through ε.
A left dual has evaluation V*⊗V→k and coevaluation k→V⊗V*, with action (h·f)(v)=f(S(h)v). Bijectivity of S is not assumed.
The right-dual construction assumes bijective S, uses (h·f)(v)=f(S⁻¹(h)v), and reverses the evaluation and coevaluation orientations.
V** carries the twice-applied left-dual action. Its ordinary bidual map satisfies h·j(v)=j(S²(h)v); a pivot satisfies S²(h)=php⁻¹ and gives jₚ(v)=j(pv).
The Taft convention is gx=ζxg, Δ(x)=1⊗x+x⊗g and S(x)=−xg⁻¹, with N>1, ζ primitive of order N and char(k) not dividing N.

load_bearing.statement: For a bialgebra H, the diagonal tensor action, counit unit module, and canonical associator and unit maps define a monoidal category of left H-modules. Conversely, the stated module-action and canonical-map H-linearity conditions for all modules recover the bialgebra axioms. No symmetry or braiding is asserted.

For a finite-dimensional left module V over a bialgebra with antipode S, the candidate action makes V* a left module; evaluation and coevaluation are H-linear and the two triangle composites are identities. No bijectivity of S is assumed.
The category has all unital left H-modules and H-linear maps, with candidate tensor action h·(v⊗w)=Σh₍₁₎v⊗h₍₂₎w and candidate unit action h·c=ε(h)c.

Bijective S supplies the stated right dual. The ordinary bidual map is H-linear exactly when S²(h) and h act identically on the given module. Involutivity suffices on every finite-dimensional module, with the converse asserted when H is finite-dimensional. An invertible group-like pivot gives a natural monoidal bidual isomorphism.

concerns.concern: Fact F4 attributes “v^i(v_j)=δij, and the dual basis spans V*” to def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional. That supplier only defines linear functionals and the algebraic dual with pointwise operations; it does not state the finite dual-basis theorem. The assertion is correct and follows immediately from the displayed finite basis, but the cited source does not contain the attributed result.
